comment: Every identity permitted to author or commit in this repository.
This is an allowlist, deliberately, and not a list of banned addresses. The
incident that produced it involved one corporate address the owner knew about;
auditing the history for it turned up a second corporate domain from a former
employer that nobody had thought to look for. A denylist only ever blocks the
leak someone already noticed. An allowlist blocks the one nobody has.
Both `author` and `committer` are checked. They differ on rebases, amends, and
web merges, so validating one leaves the other free to carry anything.
Commits reachable from this one are out of scope. Twenty-one of them carry a
non-approved corporate identity across two domains, and they are already on
`main` — rewriting the default branch would invalidate every clone and open
pull request while leaving the old objects reachable by SHA on the forge
anyway, so the rewrite would not actually remove the data.
Recorded here rather than left implicit. A check whose scope silently begins
partway through history reads as proof the whole history is clean, and this
history is not. Anything after this commit is enforced with no exceptions.
